extra.message: Student.create() builds the INSERT query via Python % string formatting with the 'name' value, which comes directly from the unauthenticated POST parameter data['name'] in views.students (sqli/views.py:55-57). The formatted string is passed to cur.execute() with no parameter binding, allowing arbitrary SQL injection.

Jinja2 is configured with autoescape=False, so all template variables are rendered unescaped. User-controlled values stored in the DB (student names, course titles/descriptions, review texts) are rendered in templates such as course.jinja2 ({{ review.review_text }}), students.jinja2 ({{ name }}) and courses.jinja2 ({{ course.title }}), enabling stored cross-site scripting.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The csrf_middleware is commented out of the middleware chain, so although forms include a _csrf_token field, the token is never validated server-side. All state-changing POST endpoints (login, add student, add course, review, evaluate) are vulnerable to cross-site request forgery.

The students view handles POST by creating a new student (Student.create at line 57) but has no @authorize decorator, while the template only renders the creation form for authenticated users (students.jinja2 '{% if auth_user %}'). Any unauthenticated attacker can POST to /students/ to create students (also the SQL injection entry point).

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The courses view handles POST by creating a new course (Course.create at lines 89-90) with no @authorize(ensure_admin=True) check, even though courses.jinja2 only shows the creation form to admins ('{% if auth_user and auth_user.is_admin %}'). Any unauthenticated or non-admin user can create courses by POSTing to /courses/.

The evaluate view assigns marks to students via POST /students/{student_id}/evaluate/{course_id} with no @authorize(ensure_admin=True) check, although course.jinja2 only displays the evaluation form to admins ('{% if auth_user.is_admin %}'). Any unauthenticated user can assign/overwrite grades.

Passwords are verified by comparing against an unsalted MD5 hex digest (md5(password.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()). MD5 is a fast, broken hash and unsalted digests are trivially crackable with rainbow tables, exposing all user passwords if the database is compromised.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort
CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: The Redis-backed session storage is created with httponly=False, so the session cookie is readable from JavaScript. Combined with the stored XSS (autoescape=False), an attacker can steal session cookies and hijack accounts, including the admin.

handle_50x passes the caught exception object into the errors/50x.jinja2 template, which renders '{{ error.__dict__ }}' (line 6). Internal exception details (including request data, headers, and potentially SQL/DSN fragments) are disclosed to end users.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The aiohttp Application is created with debug=True unconditionally. Debug mode can leak verbose diagnostic information and should never be enabled in production.

Hardcoded PostgreSQL credentials (user 'postgres', password 'postgres') are committed in the default config loaded by sqli/app.py (default_config='./config/dev.yaml'). Weak, version-controlled database credentials enable unauthorized DB access.

Seed data creates accounts with well-known credentials: 'superadmin'/'superadmin' (admin), 'j.doe'/'password', 's.king'/'password', 'p.parker'/'spidey'. These hardcoded default credentials allow trivial authentication bypass / admin takeover on any deployed instance.
